_comment: EV6: every civilian building, composed from the Medieval Village MegaKit (D24 -- the one architectural family). Each prefab is a recipe: modules in LOCAL metres (origin = footprint centre at ground level, front = +z), assembled once by scripts/world/building_prefabs.gd and duplicated per placement. The kit is authored at real scale on a 2m wall grid (walls 2.0w x 3.12h, measured); no scale corrections anywhere. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_vocabulary: Bible sec12's material grade: pale plaster + warm timber for homes, uneven stone for working buildings, ONE roof family (round terracotta tiles) across the whole settlement -- the old three-family mess (BLOCKED.md, resolved by D24) is exactly what a second roof material would reinvite. Gable fronts face the viewer's approach; chimneys break the ridge line; every building sits on a low RockTrim border skirt so it meets the grass in stone, not in a hard plaster line (bible secE).
_comment_colliders: A prefab with no `colliders` gets one combined-AABB box from the placer, same as the old farm pack. The workshop authors its own so the open arch bay is genuinely enterable -- an open doorway with an invisible wall across it is the hologram village.gd's own header warns about, from the other side.

well._why_retint: round 3 (EV6-remainder-well-rocktrim-shadow): rounds 1-2 kept pushing the colour multiply warmer and it kept not closing the gap, because colour was never the real defect -- MI_RockTrim imports with metallic=1.0 (confirmed via tools/_probe_rocktrim_material.gd), a bare-metal value no stone surface wants, versus the adjacent paving's MI_UnevenBrick at a correct metallic=0.0. Under the Compatibility renderer's realtime-only lighting (no reflection probes), a full-metal surface has almost no diffuse ambient response, so it goes flat and cold in shadow while a dielectric neighbour in the identical shadow reads normally warm -- exactly the asymmetry the round-2 critic named. Fixed at the actual layer: metallic forced to 0.0 through a new optional key on the retint schema (building_prefabs.gd::_apply_retint), keeping round 2's warm colour rather than reverting it.

inn._why: R7.9, owner-requested 2026-08-16: an inn where the villagers can stay. No inn/tavern prefab exists in the Medieval Village MegaKit (D24 -- the one civilian architectural family), so this clones farmhouse_shell's own two-storey massing -- the closest existing shape, per the backlog item's own text -- rather than inventing an off-family landmark (village.json's own note on the removed TowerWindmill records exactly why that would repeat D24's split-the-difference failure). Unlike farmhouse_shell this authors a real openable door leaf and wall colliders with a doorway hole (R7.8's door verb, scripts/world/village_door.gd), because an inn is entered by strangers on an ordinary interact, not gated by a story beat the way Grandpa's is. Footprint 6m (x) by 10m (z), front = +z. The interior (scripts/world/inn_interior.gd, attached by village.gd from village.json's `interior: "inn"` key) caps the walkable space at the FIRST storey only -- a flat ceiling collider blocks the upper course and roof shell, which stays facade-only. A real second floor is Grandpa's one bespoke cost in this settlement (loft, stairs, rail) and an ordinary inn does not obviously owe the same investment just because its shell is two storeys.

inn._why_retint: warm pane, same colour every other building in the square carries. MI_RoundTiles retint (confirmed the real material name with a throwaway probe loading the .gltf module directly and printing every surface's resource_name, per ralph/NOTES.md's own R7.9 record) was written as 'the whole of how it reads as its own building rather than a second copy of the farmhouse shell'. HIST-164 is the finding that it was not enough, and it is measurable rather than a matter of taste: the inn and farmhouse_shell have IDENTICAL module histograms -- 74 modules against 75, and the one extra is a door leaf, which is not visible from outside -- so a blind critic reading a frame of the two side by side called them 'visible twins in the same frame' and concluded 'the world cannot be navigated by looking at it'. MI_WoodTrim (dark stained oak) and MI_Plaster (a warm limewash) are added because half-timbering is the dominant texture on both buildings, so those two named surfaces are what change how the whole facade reads, where the roof alone changes one band of it. Named surfaces, not art.json's single multiply over every surface, which MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC sec21 names as the failure. STILL OPEN, and recorded rather than buried: the massing is unchanged -- same footprint, same roof module, same window pattern -- which is the other half of what 'the same kit used the same way twice' means. See ralph/reports/hist-clusters-log.md for what an L-plan would cost and why four dormers were tried and rejected.

castle._why: RE-MASSED 2026-08-16, owner directive (second playtest): the OF4-rebuild castle read as 'toys in a field' -- 23x17m, 3.9m walls, 6.2m tallest tower against a 1.8m player -- and the owner asked for concept-board scale (docs/reference/owner-board-2026-08-15-*.png, castle panels), rebuilt IN PLACE so the stronghold complex behind it (stronghold.json's five chambers, gauntlet and climax, all sited against this footprint's south edge) stands exactly where it was. The south curtain keeps the shipped gate line z=-8.448 for that reason. Footprint 36x40m on the wall centrelines -- the terrain chose that bound, not timidity: the Rise flank climbs +34m twenty metres west of the wall and the heightfield ends ~30m east (measured, probe grid 2026-08-16), so HEIGHT carries the scale instead: 10.2m two-course curtains at module scale 2.6, 19.4m corner towers, 14.2m twin gatehouse flankers, and a ~29m keep. Generated layout (uniform runs), authored landmarks -- the same author-time-recipe philosophy as before, with the generator's constants recorded here.
castle._why_colliders: The old castle had NO colliders anywhere -- you walked through the walls of the endgame landmark. Every wall run, tower and the keep now carries a box in `colliders`, the same {at,size} local-space format village.gd already consumes; landmark.gd builds the StaticBody. The gate bay is deliberately OPEN (the passage is real now, the courtyard is walkable plinth, and the gate-shadow slab is retired), and the plinth + entry ramp colliders are landmark.gd's own, since both are its geometry.
castle._why_course_seam: OF4-gate-arch (2026-08-13): the upper course sits at y=1.408, not the 1.549 OF4-rebuild shipped. 1.549 is WallBricks' full height INCLUDING its crenellations, and every wall variant in this kit is crenellated -- so stacking a second course on the first left the lower course's crenel notches (that module is solid to y=1.408 and open from 1.408 to 1.563) as a continuous row of daylight slots punched straight through the curtain at mid-height: in the gate-side frames it read as a dotted bright line running the whole wall, and again on the far wall seen through the gate itself. Seating the upper course at 1.408 buries those notches behind it. Costs 0.14m of wall height (3.90m -> 3.76m) and turns the lower parapet into a proud string course, which is what a two-course curtain wants to look like anyway.
castle._why_gate_jamb_filler: STRONGHOLD-R2. THE VERTICAL SKY SLOT IN THE SOUTH FACE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A HOLE IN THE WALL. `gate-close` came back with a narrow strip of open sky running the full height of the frame just outside the gate's right jamb -- you could see straight through the fortress. Nothing is missing from the curtain: tools/_probe_castle_gaps.gd measured every module in the castle's own frame and the south run is continuous from x -17.99 to -2.02. The slot is PARALLAX. The gatehouse flankers stand 1.5m proud of the curtain (their south face is z -10.79, the gate block's is -9.27) and each flanker is a HOLLOW tower, so from any eye off the gate's own axis -- and the gate-close eye is off it, the bay is at x +2 and the camera at x 0 -- there is a wedge of directions that passes INSIDE the flanker's near edge (x -1.421) and OUTSIDE the gate block's (x -1.400) and meets nothing until the sky above the far wall. Measured: the wedge runs from tan 0.1534 to tan 0.1867 off the view axis, i.e. screen px 719..736 of 1280, which is exactly the slot. The four filler modules at the end of `modules` stand 0.2m NORTH of the curtain plane (z -8.248 against the run's -8.448, so they can never z-fight it) inside the flankers' own hollows, and reach x -1.0 / +5.0 -- past both jambs, closing the wedge with ~0.4m of margin where a filler in the curtain's own plane would have had 0.009m and failed on the next camera nudge. They are invisible from every other direction: the curtain hides them from the south, the flanker from the sides, and 0.2m of one pokes into the courtyard at the gatehouse's base, where a pilaster belongs anyway. The +x side gets the mirrored pair because the same wedge opens there for any eye on that side of the axis; it is closed in THIS frame only because this camera happens to sit toward -x.
castle._why_retint: every material in the kit's own MTLs (LightRock/DarkRock/Black/Celing/LightWood/Banner, all variants) exports at the same placeholder grey Kd (0.64,0.64,0.64) -- a real gap in this particular pack's Blender export, confirmed directly against the OBJ/MTL text, not a design choice. Retint gives each material-name slot the stone/timber/iron/heraldic tone its name implies, the same surface-name convention village.gd's own retint (MI_WindowGlass above) already uses.

castle._why_retint_backlit: GATE-E-STRONGHOLD-ART (2026-08-23). Every stone value in this block was raised roughly one and a half stops; the value LADDER between them is unchanged. Two blind critics called the stronghold 'untextured', 'unlit-looking', 'a flat black slab', and the cause is not a broken material path -- it is that these albedos were chosen against a LIT face and the player never sees one. The sun is authored at pitch -44/yaw -40 (data/config/art.json), which puts it in the NORTH sky; the ramp, the gate and the whole approach are on the SOUTH side (landmark.gd::_build_ramp), so the hero face of the endgame landmark is backlit at every hour the chapter is played, lit by ambient alone. Measured on main with tools/frame_stats.py: near-field luma 0.012 on `gate-close` and 0.053 on `silhouette-approach`, against the 0.49-0.60 this file's own art.json comments quote from the Palworld references -- ten to forty times under. An albedo of #786d5e under ambient-only fill lands near black no matter how correct it looks in a lit test render. The earlier pass that DARKENED these (recorded in landmark.gd's PLINTH_COLOUR history) was answering a washed-out-at-distance complaint from the era when this was a long-range wayfinding silhouette; OF13 moved the site out of long-range view entirely and landmark.gd's own header says that argument is no longer load-bearing, so the darkening it bought can be given back. `Black` is lifted off near-void for the same reason: an absolute black reads as a hole in the render rather than as a shadowed recess. Banner keeps Team Tether's reserved oxblood untouched. TUNABLE, and the first thing to re-check if the stronghold ever reads washed out from a genuinely sunlit angle.
castle._why_retint_panel_noise: STRONGHOLD-R2. `DarkRock` #6b5f52 -> #8b7c6b and `Black` #221d18 -> #3a3229. The blind critique on the round-1 frames named 'noise-rectangle windows floating mid-wall, some half over edges'. They are not decals and nothing is misplaced: `WallBricks`/`TallWallBricks` carry their brick panels in DarkRock and their openings in Black, and at a stop and a half below the LightRock face those panels stopped reading as masonry and started reading as rectangles pasted onto a blank wall -- the eye sorts a high-contrast rectangle on an otherwise flat field as a separate OBJECT, not as texture. Closing the gap (DarkRock now about 0.6 of a stop under LightRock instead of ~1.5; Black lifted further off void, the same move round 1 made for the same reason) puts them back into the same surface. The value LADDER is unchanged and still holds in both directions: LightRock #a3907a > DarkRock #8b7c6b > Black #3a3229 > landmark.gd's PLINTH_COLOUR #524a41, so the foundation is still the darkest stone on the site and still grounds the mass. This does NOT fix a window that straddles a module boundary -- that is the gatehouse flanker overlapping the curtain run, and closing it needs the massing re-authored, not a colour -- it stops that window being the loudest thing on the wall. TUNABLE; if the castle ever reads flat and detail-less at range, this pair is the first place to widen again.
castle._why_retint_metallic: T1-CASTLE (2026-08-29). Every material in this kit's MTLs -- not just the albedo `_why_retint` already found flat -- shares the identical placeholder block (`Ks 0.500000`), confirmed by direct probe of the imported StandardMaterial3D: LightRock and DarkRock both come in at `metallic=0.5, roughness=1.0`. That is the exact same class of kit-export gap `BASELINE_RETINT` above already found and fixed for `MI_RockTrim` (a different, glTF kit) -- Godot's OBJ importer has no specular workflow to put `Ks` into, so it lands in `metallic` instead, and a half-metal dielectric-shaped surface with no reflection probes (Compatibility renderer, real-time lighting only) has nowhere to put the specular half of its response, so it renders desaturated and value-flattened relative to real stone/wood/cloth -- a real, measurable contributor to the owner's 'pale, flat, plastic/toylike' verdict on the castle up close (`ralph/OWNER_FEEDBACK_2026-08-29_BUILDINGS.md`), independent of the albedo values `_why_retint`/`_why_retint_backlit`/`_why_retint_panel_noise` already tuned. Every material name in the kit (`Banner` included -- cloth has no more business being half-metal than stone does) gets `metallic: 0.0` here; nothing else in this block changes.
castle._why_retint_hall_design: T1-HALL-BUILD (2026-08-30), `ralph/reports/HALL_DESIGN_2026-08-30.md` §5. The metallic fix above corrected the specular gap but not the diagnosis: the judge measured the lit wall at (212,203,185) -- essentially off-white, whiter than the tan `#a3907a` albedo intended, because a flat colour multiplied by nothing still has nowhere to put shape. `landmark.gd::_weather_castle` now multiplies these slots by the works' own real `T_UnevenBrick` photo texture (identical to `stronghold.gd`'s wall material) instead of a generated grayscale multiply, and these colours are re-derived against that texture's measured ~0.49 average luminance (design doc's pre-multiplied arithmetic) so the SAME visual target lands through a texture instead of through a flat value. `Black` drops out of the texture pass (design table: 'flat', voids/iron should not read as quarried stone) and keeps a flat retint at a slightly lighter value so a shaded opening stays a shadowed recess rather than a void. Kill criteria (design §5/§11): lit wall patch mean in [150,185], patch std-dev ≥ 35 -- pixel-sampled from `_judge_capture_arch_0829.gd`'s own stands before this is trusted.

meadows_hall._why_towers_t1_hall_rebuild: OWNER, 2026-08-30, on the first T1-HALL-REBUILD frames: the mid-wall tower "between the two parts of the castle" is "the untextured beige hut thing" and "looks like shit". That is a real property of the module, not a tuning miss. `WatchTowerWRoof.obj` is built ENTIRELY from the kit's `Celing` and `LightWood` slots -- probed directly, those are the only two `usemtl` lines in the file -- and carries no stone slot at all. `stronghold.gd`'s `HALL_WEATHER_MATERIALS` pass, the thing that puts real `T_UnevenBrick` on this kit (which ships zero UVs and placeholder-grey materials), is stone-only by design, so this module can NEVER receive a texture from it. No retint, scale or placement fixes a flat beige hut on stilts standing at the joint of a coursed-stone fortress; the module had to go. All four instances (gatehouse guard post, the two mid-wall towers, the great tower's north-east corner) are now `LargeSquareTowerBricks` -- `LightRock.001`/`DarkRock`/`Black.001`, and therefore textured by that same pass; it is the module every tower in the frames that reads as real masonry already uses. Scales preserve the design's own girth rule (native girth 1.288-1.371, measured off the OBJ): the mid-wall pair at 3.15 gives 4.06-4.32m against the corner towers' 3.86-4.11m at 3.0, so mid-wall girth still EXCEEDS corner girth -- the direct fix for the judge's 'sandcastle decoration' finding -- and the taller mid-wall shaft adds the roofline break the 400m stand wants. The guard post drops to 2.6 to stay subordinate to the 3.4 gatehouse flankers; the great tower's north-east corner takes 4.0 so it still steps down from its three 5.2 siblings. The `Banner` module goes with them, same owner pass, same verdict: see `stronghold.gd::_hang_banner`, which now builds hanging cloth instead of standing the kit's toy pennant on a stick.
meadows_hall._why_silhouette_t1_hall_3: T1-HALL-3, 2026-08-30, answering JUDGE-5 D3 (ranked 3rd of 16) -- read blind: "the entire stronghold is a pale ~60px smudge ... smaller and lower-contrast than the tether pylons flanking it, which read first ... a single symmetric mass on a bald hill, one roofline, no towers breaking upward". Measured against the authored scales, the judge is describing an arithmetic fact: of the 18 massing modules, 13 stood between 12.5m and 14.4m above the floor, so there was effectively ONE roofline, and the only masses that broke it (the great tower group) sat at the far south-west corner where every nearer mass occludes them from the north approach. This pass buys the silhouette with SCALE and PLACEMENT, not with modules: the count stays 18 and the draw calls stay flat, which the lane's inherited draw-call overrun (2706 against a 2463 ceiling) makes non-negotiable. Heights above floor now ladder 10.8 / 12.5 / 14.2 (gatehouse, unchanged and deliberately the LOW near mass) / 15.0 / 16.7 (bailey) / 20.7 (arena) / 22.5 / 26.7 (great tower corners) / 37.7 (the spire) -- the design's own "masses step DOWN eastward" and "the roofline must break at least four times" (HALL_DESIGN sec3), which the previous build did not deliver. The spire also moves from the legendary chamber's SOUTH-west corner to its NORTH-west one, where the west shoulder still backs it (the probed shoulder runs z 7546-7602, which is the NORTH half of the site) but the arriving player can actually see it. This deliberately exceeds HALL_DESIGN sec3's "+27...+33 absolute" cap for the tower caps: that number produced the building the judge could not find, and the spire now tops out near +44. The design's stated INTENT -- a landmark legible from the approach -- wins over its arithmetic, and the deviation is recorded here rather than left for the next lane to rediscover.
